caveats: sha256_bench measures SHA-256 alone, a best case for Zknh; programs that hash little gain little.
The std objects are built for rv32i in every variant (the GCC 12.2 crash with Zbs on std/src/helperfunctions.c); they only print, outside the timed windows.
sha256_long is not run at -O0: at about 213 cycles per byte it would take over 200 million cycles, more than three minutes of simulation.
GCC 12.2 has no builtins for the Zknh instructions: zknh.h issues them by inline assembly, and rev8 is inline assembly as well (GCC 12 does not emit it on RV32).

The cycles are those of the Verilator model of the RTL of this working tree. The RTL has not been implemented on an FPGA since the Zbb, Zbs and Zicond unit was added, nor since the cryptography half, so whether it still meets 50 MHz is unknown.
